nyciml-2009-10-fall-sophfrosh-02.prompt: One leg of a right triangle is length 20. The lengths of the other leg and the hypotenuse are consecutive odd integers. Compute the length of the hypotenuse.

nyciml-2009-10-fall-sophfrosh-03.prompt: Compute the two-digit number that is 9 times the sum of its digits.

nyciml-2009-10-fall-sophfrosh-04.prompt: A boat can travel 8 miles per hour in still water. If it can travel 15 miles with the current in the same time it travels 9 miles against the current, compute the rate of the current in miles per hour.

nyciml-2009-10-fall-sophfrosh-05.prompt: There are 4 different science, 3 different math and 2 different history books on a shelf. Compute the number of ways they can be arranged if all the books on the same subject have to be next to each other.

nyciml-2009-10-fall-sophfrosh-06.prompt: $ABCD$ is a rectangle and $P$ is a point inside the rectangle. If $PA=3$, $PB=4$, $PC=5$, compute $PD$.

nyciml-2009-10-fall-sophfrosh-07.prompt: Compute the remainder when $777^{777}$ is divided by 5.

nyciml-2009-10-fall-sophfrosh-08.prompt: A sphere with radius 5 is cut by a plane which is 3 units from the center of the sphere. Compute the area of the cross-section formed.

nyciml-2009-10-fall-sophfrosh-09.prompt: Compute the largest prime factor of $9{,}991$.

nyciml-2009-10-fall-sophfrosh-10.prompt:
If $a, b, c, x, y$, and $z$ are real numbers such that
$$\begin{aligned}ax+by+cz&=5\\ bx+cy+az&=50\\ cx+ay+bz&=500\end{aligned}$$
and $a+b+c=5$, compute $x+y+z$.

nyciml-2009-10-fall-sophfrosh-11.prompt: Compute the area of a rectangle whose diagonal is of length 10 and whose length is 5 times its width.

nyciml-2009-10-fall-sophfrosh-12.prompt: When the numbers 551, 613 and 768 are divided by $a$, $a>1$ and an integer, they leave a remainder of $b$. Compute $b$.

nyciml-2009-10-fall-sophfrosh-14.prompt: Compute the positive value of $x$ such that $x[x]=55$. (Note that $[x]$ denotes the greatest integer that is less than or equal to $x$. For example, $[1.99]=1$, and $[2]=2$.)

nyciml-2009-10-fall-sophfrosh-16.prompt: An old printing press can print a newspaper in 10 hours. A new printing press can print a newspaper in 8 hours. Working together, compute how many hours would it take 3 old and 2 new presses to print a newspaper?

nyciml-2009-10-fall-sophfrosh-17.prompt: If $100!$ is multiplied out, how many zeroes does it end with?

nyciml-2009-10-fall-sophfrosh-18.prompt: In right triangle $ABC$, $\angle C$ is a right angle, $M$ is the midpoint of $AC$, $N$ is the midpoint of $BC$. If $AN=12$ and $BM=14$, compute $AB$.
